clusters.name: St Johann / Novartis Campus
clusters.occupancyRead: Active global headquarters and biomedical R&D campus with external-company offices, an innovation-park coworking operation and the occupied FMI research building. Building 210 is currently marketed for office occupation, but no dated available-floor schedule or vacant area is disclosed. The 2025 filing's St. Johann site-size figure is not tenant-occupied or leasable area. No verified St. Johann closure, giveback or 2025/2026 new-building delivery is established. Breakthrough remains a dated, unverified project lead; IOB's current visiting address is elsewhere in Basel.
functions: Global headquarters and international commercial-unit headquarters
Corporate, operations and global support functions
Healthtech coworking, private offices and innovation support
Shared FMI–Novartis organoid and automated cellular-screening laboratory platform
Public science exhibition, meetings and events at Novartis Pavillon

clusters.detailedNarrative:
# St Johann / Novartis Campus  -  Basel-Stadt

St. Johann is an active headquarters and biomedical-research campus, with external-company offices, an innovation-park coworking operation and the occupied Friedrich Miescher Institute for Biomedical Research building. The actionable property lead is the existing Building 210 office offer, not a verified new laboratory development or quantified vacancy. No source reviewed establishes a St. Johann closure, released building, sublease or new-building delivery during 2025/2026. Novartis’s Swiss manufacturing reconfiguration announcement concerns Schweizerhalle and Stein; its Basel dateline is not a St. Johann property event. [SJ01] [SJ02] [SJ04] [SJ11] [SJ18]

**Canton BS; municipality Basel. Research cutoff 4 November 2026.** The cluster retains aerial ID `basel-st-johann-novartis-campus`, Novartis company ID `gco_9328b082a7756ed365fb` and site ID `basel:site:novartis-basel`. The full address, building, resident-reference and figure schedules are in the accompanying [St. Johann JSON record]([retained internal document] This is every verified address identified in the reviewed material, not an exhaustive tenancy census; no public coverage denominator is established.

## Occupier inventory

Novartis’s current directory attributes **Fabrikstrasse 2, Novartis Campus, CH-4056 Basel** to Novartis Pharma AG / Biomedical Research. The campus operator independently uses it as the general campus arrival address. It therefore supports research presence and campus orientation, but does not establish a particular Novartis AG legal-entity suite or the laboratories behind the gate. The group’s documented functions are global headquarters, international commercial headquarters and R&D, with operations and global support functions also identified in the company’s Swiss site profile. [SJ02] [SJ16] [SJ17]

The directory also verifies separate addresses that must not be collapsed into Fabrikstrasse 2. Novartis International AG and Novartis Pharma AG’s Pharmaceuticals entry are at **Forum 1, Novartis Campus, CH-4056 Basel**. Novartis Holding AG is **c/o Novartis International AG at Forum 1**: this is a corporate address, not evidence of a separately occupied tenancy. Novartis Pharma Services AG is at **Lichtstrasse 35, CH-4056 Basel**. These entities are retained under the existing Novartis group ID; no new global company master is created. Their individual office areas, floors, employee counts, tenure and commercial terms remain unknown. [SJ02]

Ultragenyx’s current company directory identifies its **EMEA headquarters at WSJ 210/11, Lichtstrasse 35, Postfach 3775, 4002 Basel**. The building/location code is preserved exactly, not translated into an invented suite. This is an office/HQ function; the same directory separately labels its US gene-therapy research and manufacturing sites. No Swiss wet-laboratory or manufacturing capability should be assigned from that global company activity. The existing Ultragenyx profile ID is `gco_ab05462572077b994707`; no existing Basel site ID was found in V6. [SJ10]

SOTIO Biotech AG’s Swiss contact page gives **Lichtstrasse 35 – WSJ-210, 4056 Basel** and provides business-development and clinical-department contacts. It does not identify an occupied floor, wet laboratory or manufacturing operation. FoRx Therapeutics AG gives **Lichtstrasse 35, 4056 Basel** as its current company contact address. FoRx’s address and the operator’s campus reference support a campus-associated company contact, but not a separately measured office or laboratory. Neither company has a matched V6 profile in the reviewed snapshot; both remain sourced additional canton-inventory records. Local staff, tenure, rents and lease expiries are gaps, not zero. [SJ08] [SJ09] [SJ06]

Switzerland Innovation Park Basel Area AG operates the campus’s furnished private offices and fixed-desk coworking. Its site address is **Lichtstrasse 35, 4002 Basel**, distinct from its Allschwil headquarters. The operator explicitly offers domiciliation, which is important when interpreting residents’ company addresses. A postal address here can represent a fixed desk, private office or domicile rather than a standalone suite. The dated operator article reported opening the **15th coworking floor on 24 July 2024** and moving the DayOne accelerator team there. This is a source-backed historical floor action, not a 2025/2026 expansion announcement. Current floors and their area need reconfirmation. [SJ06] [SJ07]

ISS Facility Services AG is identified in the public campus brochure as responsible for real-estate and facility-management services. That makes ISS the appropriate management contact for floor schedules and an offer, but does not establish ISS as owner or landlord. A separate ISS onsite street address, legal leasing authority and mandate period are not disclosed. [SJ05] (p. 11)

## Campus and building schedule

The Annual Report 2025 discloses **481,448 m² for “Basel, Switzerland – St. Johann”** under the heading **“Size of site, in square meters.”** Scope is the Novartis-reported St. Johann major facility; period is the 2025 year-end filing baseline, published 3 February 2026 and observed 4 November 2026. This is a primary filing-reported figure. The table does not define it as land area, gross floor area, net area or leasable space. It is not a tenant-area estimate, campus vacancy or a figure to allocate among Novartis and third-party companies. The filing’s general statement that facilities are owned or held under long-term leases does not disclose St. Johann’s specific tenure or legal title. [SJ01] (PDF p. 44 / printed p. 40)

## Availability evidence

Building 210 is currently marketed by the campus operator for offices and meeting rooms. Its live page gives **17 floors, 720 m² average floor size and 2.8 m average storey height**. Publication date is unknown; these are primary operator-reported facts observed on **4 November 2026**, not an occupied-floor count or vacancy measure. The company addresses using WSJ-210 support the Lichtstrasse 35 association, but the building/code/cadastral crosswalk still needs operator confirmation. Do not multiply the floor count by average floor size to construct a total building area. [SJ04] [SJ09] [SJ10]

The currently linked public brochure gives an **example floor plate of approximately 723 m²** and an **example subdivision of approximately 360 m²**, with the latter described as “max floor sub-division.” These are example-layout specifications, not available suite sizes. Its PDF was created in September 2021 and modified **7 April 2026**; the filename’s 2026 designation is not proof that all specifications were newly surveyed. The webpage average and brochure example are different bases and are kept separate. [SJ05] (pp. 9–10)

The brochure describes ready-to-use office fit-out supplied **as is**, with adaptations at the tenant’s cost; Ethernet/fiber infrastructure, badge-controlled separation and air ventilation are described. The live page identifies included maintenance, cleaning, security, post, waste and visitor parking, with optional services. None of this establishes laboratory ventilation capacity, electrical redundancy, containment approvals or GMP readiness. The floor-load label in the brochure is not adopted as engineering capacity because its area denominator is absent. No dated vacant-floor list, building rent, actual offered suite or handover date is disclosed. [SJ04] [SJ05]

SIP’s current live page advertises private offices **starting from CHF 1,400/month** and fixed-desk coworking **starting from CHF 360/month**. Scope is the Novartis Campus workspace offer; publication date is unknown and observation is **4 November 2026**. These are current advertised starting prices, not signed lease rents. Office size, VAT and cost inclusions, deposits and available inventory are not stated on the page. They must not be converted into CHF/m²/year or compared directly with laboratory rents. Monthly-contract wording is documented in the **July 2024 article**, not verified as a 2026 contract term. The live page’s linked older PDFs do not establish today’s free units. [SJ06] [SJ07]

## Property due diligence

The next steps are specific evidence requests, not assumptions about market demand:

1. **Obtain a dated Building 210 floor schedule from Novartis/ISS.** Require current occupiers, vacant/committed floors, actual offered units, measurement basis, office sizes, condition and move-in dates. Request a commercial offer with service inclusions and tenant-work obligations.
2. **Establish legal property interests.** Obtain parcel numbers and land-register/title extracts, building rights, encumbrances and the owner’s authority for ISS to lease. Campus branding and Novartis affiliation are not legal-owner evidence.
3. **Verify physical occupation by company.** Resolve Ultragenyx’s WSJ 210/11 designation, SOTIO’s onsite Swiss functions and occupied floor, FoRx’s office versus domicile and any separate lab, and the Novartis entities’ actual departmental allocation. Tenant areas, local employees, tenure, rent and expiry require tenancy documents or company confirmation.
4. **Check engineering and areas before underwriting laboratory use.** Obtain measured GFA/NLA/leasable schedules and the filing’s site-size definition. For Building 210 require current as-builts, clear-height definition, power/ventilation/load data, fire strategy and any lab-conversion permission. For FMI/ATMC obtain the area split, containment approvals and operating/servicing responsibilities.
5. **Resolve the development lead before putting it into a pipeline.** Ask Novartis/Breakthrough for scheme existence, address/parcels, sponsor and legal agreement, permit reference, approved area, funding, construction phase and delivery/availability timetable. Stop at “unverified” until these exist.
6. **Obtain an operator occupancy denominator.** Request residents by actual office/fixed desk versus domicile and current floor, then verify their company addresses. Resolve IOB’s contradictory operator reference and BDSS’s actual operating address separately.
7. **Match official building-register addresses before street-level pins.** Internal campus addresses, postal codes and company location codes need a cadastral crosswalk; no tenant or lease polygon is inferred from the existing image.

clusters.detailedNarrative:
# Roche / Kleinbasel  -  Basel-Stadt

Roche’s Kleinbasel campus is an active headquarters, pharmaceutical research and development, and synthetic-molecule development/launch-production location undergoing internal consolidation and reinvestment. The operating pRED complex and the newly inaugurated Building 92 must be separated from Building 12 and the Synthetic Molecules Facility construction program. Older south-site buildings are being emptied and dismantled for Roche’s own redevelopment; that does not establish a third-party leasing opportunity or a quantified reduction in the company’s occupied area. Research cutoff: 4 November 2026. [RK01] [RK04] [RK05] [RK06] [RK08] [RK09]

This record covers Basel municipality in canton BS. It excludes Rosental Mitte, Roche Kaiseraugst in Aargau and Roche Grenzach-Wyhlen in Germany. Combined Basel/Kaiseraugst disclosures are not allocated to Kleinbasel. The retained identifiers are company **`gco_452de3e48d5e8b37d3d5`**, site **`basel:site:roche-basel`**, and aerial **`basel-roche-kleinbasel`**. These come from the supplied source-safe V6 snapshot, captured 4 November 2026, and the retained Basel aerial records; neither master was modified.

## Occupier inventory

The verified street address is **F. Hoffmann-La Roche AG, Konzern-Hauptsitz, Grenzacherstrasse 124, CH-4070 Basel, Switzerland**. Roche publishes it on its current Basel R&D location page. It is a headquarters/campus contact reference, not proof of an individual building entrance, a Roche Holding AG suite or an institute’s measured occupancy. Roche Holding AG / Roche Holding Ltd is the retained group-level profile; F. Hoffmann-La Roche AG is the named physical operator. Retained V6 evidence from the 2025 Finance Report supports that corporate distinction, not property ownership. [RK01] [RK11]

Roche’s Basel research functions include discovery and early development, research informatics, research and clinical operations, clinical research, exploratory development, clinical science, safety science and regulatory affairs. Its stated research areas span oncology, neuroscience and rare diseases, cardiovascular and metabolic diseases, immunology, infectious diseases and ophthalmology. This supports a laboratory-and-office occupancy profile rather than an office-only interpretation. It does not supply a current floor-by-floor accommodation schedule. [RK01]

The Building 92 fact sheet explicitly names **Roche’s Institute of Human Biology, 360 Labs of Pharma Research and Early Development, and Pharma Technical Operations** as occupants. These are Roche institute/department references, not independent-company or external-tenant admissions. IHB uses advanced tissue cultures, organoids, organ-on-chip systems and computational modelling, combining biology, computational biology and translational bioengineering. No separate street address or occupied-area allocation was found for these programs. Academic partnerships do not establish partner residency on the campus. [RK08] [RK09]

For production, Roche describes existing synthetic-molecule development and commercial-launch operations as distributed across several buildings. The SMF project will consolidate new and retained equipment in Buildings 50 and 51. That is evidence of existing activity and a future reconfiguration, not proof that the whole new facility is already operating or that the investment equals net-new manufacturing capacity. [RK04] [RK05]

## Campus and building schedule

### Operating pRED complex: Buildings 4, 5, 6 and 7

Roche Spaces reports **58,900 m² net area** and **98,100 m² GFA** for the complete four-building pRED complex. These are source-stated property measures on an undated current primary page retrieved 4 November 2026. The measurement standard and inclusion schedule are not disclosed. Neither figure is a verified live occupied-area total, a lab-only footprint, a lease area or a whole-campus area. [RK02]

Building 4 is the convention/meeting component, with an auditorium, classrooms, meeting rooms and offices. Building 5 is the office component. Buildings 6 and 7 are interconnected high-rise laboratory/office buildings with adaptable laboratories and adjacent office zones. Their individual areas and street entrances are not disclosed in the reviewed property page. The descriptions support actual laboratory infrastructure but do not establish biosafety levels, cleanroom certification, utility capacities, floor loading or a fitted suite available to outsiders. [RK02]

The supplied **Basel Area Life Sciences Hub** extract records **110,000 m² “GF”**, with a 2024 completion label for Roche pRED-Zentrum on brochure page 23. “GF” is undefined. Its documentary date is PDF CreationDate/ModDate **31 October 2025**, not a stated publication date. This remains historical restricted-source evidence; it has not been converted to NLA or current occupied area. The primary 98,100 m² GFA and historical 110,000 m² undefined GF are retained separately because their scope and basis have not been reconciled. The private original brochure is not attached, linked or copied into this output.

### Building 92: completed reuse renovation and 2026 inauguration

Roche’s Building 92 fact sheet states **23,000 m² total floor area**, a building-wide measure with no gross/net definition or departmental allocation. The fact sheet is undated but linked from the **23 March 2026** inauguration release and was retrieved 4 November 2026. It reports renovation completion in **Q4 2025** and inauguration on **23 March 2026**. The former medical-chemistry laboratory has become the research home for IHB, alongside the other named Roche occupants. [RK08] [RK09]

The disclosed Building 92 project investment is **CHF 100 million**, from the same fact sheet. Accommodation for **up to 250 IHB researchers** is design capacity, not observed headcount, local FTE or net-new employment. The entire 23,000 m² must not be assigned to IHB alone. Modular laboratory design and reused equipment are documented; process certifications and technical accommodation specifications remain unverified. [RK08] [RK09]

### Building 50: existing asset with active refurbishment

The public **2026 SMF flyer**, exact publication date unknown and retrieved 4 November 2026, assigns **5,240 m² above-ground gross floor area** to its B50 component. It also describes Building 50 as having several sectors, only certain parts of which are being adapted. Obtain the project boundary before treating the flyer figure as the entire existing building’s area. It is not measured occupied area. [RK05]

Roche’s current construction notices give **3 November 2025** as the start of sector refurbishment, facade renovation and new ventilation installation, with that construction phase ending **Q3 2027**. This is not the completion date of the combined SMF program. The notices are undated live operator evidence observed 4 November 2026, with all schedules subject to change. [RK06]

### Other building references preserved without invented pins

The JSON keeps Building 34 as the demolished predecessor to Building 12 and Building 66 as the predecessor to new Building 51. The source also gives an internal SMF project-office routing reference, **B9/27 OG05/06, 4070 Basel**. That is not a complete street address or a separately verified commercial suite. [RK05] [RK06]

Buildings 1 and 2 are office-tower references in the official development context. Buildings 21, 27 and 52 appear in south-site planning and heritage discussions. Building 10 appears in a roof-equipment maintenance notice and Building 67 in a plaza-investigation notice; those notices do not establish their life-science accommodation or current floor occupants. All these encountered identifiers are retained in the underlying JSON as contextual records, with unverified addresses and area left null. They are not padded into new occupier rows. [RK06] [RK07]

## Development pipeline

### Building 12: replacement and consolidation, not a current delivery

Roche’s **29 October 2025** release gives **32,200 m² “building area”** for Building 12, without identifying a gross, net or usable basis. It announces approximately **CHF 500 million** of project investment and planned completion in **Q4 2029**. The building will consolidate research and development functions previously spread across the site. Its flexible pilot plant and laboratory floors support the interface between early research and development to production readiness. [RK03] [RK06]

Current operator notices distinguish structural works starting **1 September 2025**, after Building 34 demolition, from the later ceremonial groundbreaking. They describe development activity in the new building from **2030**. The design accommodates up to **450 researchers**; this is not actual FTE or a verified increase in local employment. Handover, commissioning and operational readiness are distinct milestones. No lease offer or independently certified process throughput was found. [RK03] [RK06]

### Building 51 and the SMF: construction through 2030

Roche’s **21 September 2026** release announces Building 51 groundbreaking and approximately **CHF 790 million** for the **combined new Building 51 and Building 50 modernization**, not Building 51 alone. The release and public flyer give program timing through **Q4 2030**, with facilities expected complete by 2030. Approximately **200 workplaces/expected employees** is a future program capacity, not a current local workforce observation. [RK04] [RK05]

The flyer reports **6,700 m² above-ground GFA** for Building 51. It excludes underground floors and is not a tenant or lab-only area. The new building replaces Building 66 and will accommodate synthetic-molecule development and commercial-launch production with modular equipment and digitally connected infrastructure. The current notices report demolition/excavation starting **9 February 2026**, forecast to finish **Q4 2026**; no completed excavation status is inferred at the research cutoff. [RK04] [RK05] [RK06]

Roche’s generic development overview still contains older SMF cost/timing and a different Building 12 floor count. The dated September 2026 release and 2026 project flyer control the current SMF read; the older overview is not a current delivery commitment. Do not combine those vintages into one pipeline. [RK03] [RK04] [RK05] [RK10]

### South site: internal clearance, infrastructure and conditional future buildings

The official Basel-Stadt commission report adopted **28 August 2025** describes the then-current south-site **170,400 m² Bruttogeschossfläche**, with the base planning quantum intended to remain rather than become an additive development total. This is dated official property/planning evidence, not current occupied area, available area or full-campus GFA. The report includes competing draft resolutions; it is not a certified current in-force plan. [RK07]

Roche’s current notice reports Grand Council approval of the wider redevelopment plan on **15 October 2025**. It says old unnecessary south-site buildings are already mostly emptied, with hazardous-material remediation and interior dismantling under way. Technical infrastructure remains operating to supply north-site research and production. External demolition is planned **from 2027**. A new underground heating/cooling facility beneath the lawn in front of Building 52 began in **September 2025** and is forecast to support campus supply from **summer 2027**. These are operator statements observed 4 November 2026, not independently verified building-by-building completion dates. [RK06]

Building 3 remains a possible future tower. The official 2025 report describes a vision without a concrete project or current additional-space requirement. Building 124 is a visitor/employee facility reference in the proposed south-site planning schedule. Neither is supported here as a committed construction start, laboratory delivery or third-party offer. The final plan, legal effective date and any appeals or stays require direct verification. The legal attachment located in this review could not be read and subsequently returned HTTP 404; plan approval is not treated as proof that every implementation permission is effective. [RK06] [RK07]

## Availability evidence

No dated primary offer for external letting, subletting, sale or an available fitted laboratory suite was established within the assigned Roche campus. Available area, vacancy rate, rent, lease expiry and commercial terms remain **unknown**, not zero. The pRED brochure callout was a private project/completion label, not a rental offer. Rosental offers are outside this cluster.

The practical opportunity read is campus reinvestment and possible future estate decisions, not an identified investable vacancy. Roche’s empty old south-site stock is being remediated for its own redevelopment. Its dated plans support this internal-use interpretation; they do not establish that a third party can occupy or acquire any of those buildings. No acquisition has been used as closure or giveback evidence. [RK06] [RK07]

## Property due diligence

Obtain Roche’s current building register, verified entrances, departmental accommodation schedule, cadastral parcels and title entities before placing street-level building pins. The SMF flyer identifies **F. Hoffmann-La Roche AG as “Bauherr / Owner”**. This is a disclosed project-client designation; it is not a parcel-by-parcel legal-title extract. The official south-site report describes Roche landownership, but the exact title entity and extent are still unverified. [RK05] [RK07]

Request measurement-standard-labelled land, GFA, usable/NLA and occupied-area schedules. The immediate reconciliations are pRED’s net/GFA versus the historical undefined GF, Building 92’s occupant allocation, Building 12’s unspecified “building area,” and the sector extent represented by B50’s flyer area. Obtain an SMF production/technical/basement split and phased commissioning schedule. Do not add the various property and planning totals to derive campus occupancy.

For Building 12, verify Q4 2029 handover versus 2030 operation and identify the existing accommodation it replaces. For SMF, separate B50’s Q3 2027 construction-phase end from Q4 2030 program completion. Obtain the certified effective south-site plan, appeal/stay status, demolition permissions, hazardous-material program and heritage obligations for individual buildings. Building 3 and Building 124 require committed funding, scope, consent and dates before entering a delivery pipeline.

If investment or leasing access is relevant, ask Roche explicitly whether any disposal, sale, third-party letting, sublease or external-occupier admission is contemplated. Only a dated availability schedule and terms can support that opportunity. Obtain applicable lease interests, expiry/options and rents if an external tenancy actually exists. Actual local FTE, cleanroom or biosafety classes, GMP status, power, ventilation, loading, gases, hazard constraints, redundancy and throughput remain separate evidence requests - not assumptions drawn from the word “laboratory” or “production.”

## Submarket aerials

Use retained aerial **`basel-roche-kleinbasel`** for campus orientation around Grenzacherstrasse and the Rhine. Its analytical frame is not a cadastral boundary or an occupied-area outline. Grenzacherstrasse 124 remains a campus-reference address; no new building coordinates have been generated. Verified street entrances and estate footprint geometry are the next inputs for building-level aerial and print integration. The current task has not altered the website, aerial master, shared snapshot or shared figures ledgers.

Coverage is every verified address and relevant building encountered in the stated supplied and primary evidence, not an exhaustive Roche estate census. No complete coverage denominator or current tenant register was available. The JSON preserves the full uncapped underlying inventory, contextual references, figure metadata and evidence gaps. Both project figures ledgers were checked for matching Roche/Kleinbasel entries; none was found, so new numeric provenance is held in this cluster-specific JSON rather than a shared master.

clusters.detailedNarrative:
# Rosental Mitte  -  Basel-Stadt

Rosental Mitte is an active multi-tenant chemistry, pharmaceutical-development and office location in the municipality of Basel, canton BS. It should be underwritten as an existing research/development campus with selective operator-advertised rental opportunities and a separate future building pipeline - not as a single vacant laboratory estate or a commercial biomanufacturing campus. Current primary company pages establish real operating functions, but do not disclose tenant areas or a current campus rent roll. Immobilien Basel-Stadt advertises premises in RO-1055 and RO-1059; RO-1033 is a conversion targeting early 2029, and the university targets Haus 6 occupation from 2029. The contemporaneous official release says Syngenta would rent the majority of the properties for **at least 10 years** and retain its Basel headquarters. This is historical transaction evidence dated 15 January 2019, not a building-specific expiry, a 2029 vacancy commitment or a current leased-area statement. **RO-1033  -  Sandgrubenstrasse 41, Basel.** The operator's announcement dated **13 August 2026** sets out internal demolition in 2026, conversion beginning in 2027, letting from 2027 through Immobilien Basel-Stadt, and targeted move-in at the **beginning of 2029**. Future uses are multi-tenant laboratories/offices, with entrance, meeting/function and possible service/shop uses at ground level. The top floor is office-only. The current primary page gives no floor-area quantity or granted-permit evidence. [RM06]

The supplied hub brochure, whose only identified documentary date is **PDF metadata dated 31 October 2025**, marketed WRO-1033 as **6,000 m² office/lab available from 2028**, with undefined floor-area basis. **Haus 6  -  Maulbeerstrasse, 4058 Basel, no disclosed street number.** The canton describes a planned first new-build investment for Rosental with University Chemistry and third-party rental uses, plus a publicly accessible ground floor. ## Property due diligence

The first request to **Immobilien Basel-Stadt Site Management, Frederick Stumber**, should be a dated rent roll, building-to-street-address crosswalk and room-level current availability plans. For RO-1055 and RO-1059, establish vacant versus future-release status, divisible or simultaneous offers, possession dates, rent/charges, fit-out ownership and reinstatement obligations. The public offer ranges are not enough to price a lease or measure market vacancy. [RM04] [RM05]

For **RO-1055**, obtain floor-specific load plans, lift certification, chemical-transport rules, HVAC/service capacities and accessibility constraints. For **RO-1059**, request actual room layouts, biosafety permissions, fume-hood/ventilation tests, utility allocations, hazardous-material and waste rules. Separate operator descriptions from an occupier's approved research use. [RM04] [RM05]

For **RO-1033 and Haus 6**, obtain current permit status, construction milestones, approved area schedules, servicing/subdivision drawings, pre-let process and contractual delivery protection. For Haus 6, request the university allocation, residual third-party space and numbered address. Reconcile historical quantities before any area roll-up. [RM06] [RM07] [RM08]

Ownership work should distinguish the **2016 cantonal estate** from the **2019 Syngenta/PKBS joint-venture property**, with current title, easements and any building-right interests verified building by building. Syngenta's actual lease dates, breaks and renewals are needed; the historic minimum duration is not an expiry schedule. Environmental and infrastructure work should cover soil/groundwater and building-hazard reports, remediation liability, demolition logistics and utility-tunnel easements/outage allocations. Published excavation controls are not a clean-site warranty. [RM01] [RM02] [RM20] [RM21]

For the company inventory, the unresolved cases are precise: Celonic 1033/1060; ten23 and Elanco in directory building 1094; FMI's former 1060/1063/1066; Solvias 1055/1063; ETH/C-CINA 1058; and the university's non-1096 departmental allocations. clusters.detailedNarrative:
# Klybeck / Stücki northern research corridor  -  Basel-Stadt

Stücki is an established operating cluster for drug-product development, antibody-drug conjugate research, medtech production and serviced laboratories. Klybeck combines current biotech offices and institutional research with existing offices, laboratory refurbishment and a longer-term redevelopment pipeline. The important underwriting distinction is **operating occupancy versus a marketed property programme**: current company addresses do not measure demised space, and provider/campus area figures do not establish vacancy or tenant demand. All observations below are as of **4 November 2026**; undated pages establish what is currently published, not a contemporaneous physical inspection. [KS01] [KS05] [KS06] [KS07] [KS08] [KS11]

The assigned geography is the northern corridor within the municipality of Basel, canton **BS**. Swiss Life's Campus Klybeck, Rhystadt's Neues Klybeck and Stücki Park are separate property contexts. Novartis Campus, Rosental/Roche, Allschwil and Fricktal are not imported into this inventory through proximity or brochure logos. No acquisition has been used to infer a closure.

## Occupier inventory

**Lonza Drug Product Services** publishes **Hochbergerstrasse 60 A, G, 4057 Basel** as its Stücki location. Its actual functions include parenteral formulation, analytical development and quality control, drug-product process development, testing and related manufacturing expertise. The page describes GMP quality systems; it does not establish the installed commercial aseptic capacity disclosed for Lonza's separate Stein site. Its **13,000 m² “Facility”** callout is an undated, company-reported facility measure across a grouped address, with no net/gross/lease basis or A/G allocation. It is not a measured 2026 lease demise. Retain company ID `gco_59823ff9aac271b5cc32` and site ID `basel:site:lonza-stuecki`. [KS01]

The supplied JLL/Basel Area brochure, dated **31 October 2025 by PDF metadata**, states that Lonza occupied two fully occupied Stücki buildings, **each 8,000 sqm** on page 29. That statement stays historical; the buildings are not summed into a current leased or campus aggregate. A separate primary landlord release dated **28 March 2019** described a planned additional **8,000 m²** rental in building 60G from the third quarter of 2020. These figures have different periods and bases. Neither reconciles the current facility callout or proves the origin of today's advertised space at 60A. [KS25]

**NBE-Therapeutics AG**, a Boehringer Ingelheim subsidiary, has a current company-supported address at **Hochbergerstrasse 60I, 4057 Basel**. The parent announced the completed Basel ADC R&D centre opening on **3 April 2025**. The opening's **1,826 m² of laboratories and offices** is a historical facility description, not a classified net/gross area or refreshed 2026 suite measurement. The company's contact footer and dated privacy statement support the fuller street spelling; the main contact block shortens it. Retain `gco_7a1b3460a09f20347048` / `basel:site:nbe-basel`. This is continuing Basel presence after acquisition, not an Allschwil relocation or closure. [KS02] [KS03] [KS04]

**BioVersys AG** publishes **c/o Technologiepark, Hochbergerstrasse 60c, 4057 Basel**. The existing V6 record retains headquarters and R&D; the current Tech Park directory describes antibacterial resistance research and labels the location **C3**. Preserve that operator label without decoding it into a legal suite or floor. Retain `gco_98c2776a061ff24fea05` / `basel:site:bioversys-basel`. **Medartis AG** publishes **Hochbergerstrasse 60E, 4057 Basel** for its Basel headquarters; its Basel-specific page also identifies implant-production and trovalisation imagery. That supports production-related activity, but not a quantified production plant, certified cleanroom or throughput. Retain the Medartis Holding profile `gco_b60cc392c4a72102e451` / `basel:site:medartis-basel`, with Medartis AG as the local operator. [KS05] [KS06] [KS20]

**LifeMine Therapeutics (Switzerland) GmbH** publishes **Klybeckstrasse 191, WKL-136/6. OG, 4057 Basel**. Its contact page calls Basel an additional office in the global network. Do not promote that address to a locally quantified wet-lab or manufacturing operation. Retain `gco_fb97894921c0acd2fc4b` / `basel:site:lifemine-basel`. **Monte Rosa Therapeutics AG** independently publishes **WKL-136.3, Klybeckstrasse 191, 4057 Basel**. The current contact establishes a Swiss company location, not an exact occupied area or expiry. The existing imported Monte Rosa parent profile ID `claude_csv:5c6eedfb4fa8:675` is retained as the matching parent reference; its Boston site ID is not reused for Basel. The Swiss legal-entity link needs register confirmation. [KS07] [KS08]

The historical brochure's page-28 reference to an unnamed Rhystadt building “occupied until 2027,” with Monte Rosa as an example, is not a company-specific lease-expiry disclosure. The current Tech Park homepage calls Monte Rosa an **alumnus** in its testimonial, so that testimonial is not current Stücki residency proof. [KS18]

**Superlab Suisse Basel AG** publishes **Hochbergerstr. 60 I, 4057 Basel**. The provider is an operating lab-as-a-service platform, not one biotech occupier. Swiss Prime Site's dated completed-project account confirms its service at Stücki since mid-2024. The provider's current **4,770 m² lab-and-office** callout is an undated programme footprint, not available laboratory space or the area of its members. The campus advertises BSL1/2 serviced laboratories; current licences, particular module availability and technical certificates remain request items. [KS09] [KS10] [KS11]

**Walter Klybeck** has an operating coworking/event address at **Klybeckstrasse 161, 4057 Basel, K-25**. The campus says offices have been in use since **March 2025**. Its distinct laboratory offer is in **K-410 at Klybeckstrasse 206**. The dated campus article still described that refurbishment as underway on **17 September 2026**, while the undated provider page advertises immediately usable laboratories. The correct status is **readiness unresolved**, not simply delivered or planned. Advertised **6–45 m²** plug-and-play typologies and starting charges of **CHF 1,200/month** for laboratories and **CHF 380/month** for coworking are provider service offers observed on the cutoff date, not conventional effective rents per square metre or verified available suites. [KS12] [KS13] [KS14]

The full JSON also retains **Alira Health at Hochbergerstrasse 60F** as a company-supported office address and **Tech Park Basel at Hochbergerstrasse 60C** as an infrastructure-provider address. The latter's undated **6,700 m² “Rental Area”** is the operator programme, not a vacant-space figure or a 60C-only building total. Its advertised minimum office and equipped-lab typologies are **12 m²** and **43 m²**, respectively; admission and availability require its application process. [KS16] [KS17] [KS18] [KS19]

## Institutions and operator residency

**IOB, the Institute of Molecular and Clinical Ophthalmology Basel**, is source-backed institutional research in Campus Klybeck. The institute's current **visiting and delivery address is Klybeckstrasse 141, 4057 Basel**; **Mittlere Strasse 91** is explicitly its legal-correspondence address, not this corridor's operating entrance. The campus identifies IOB with **K-420**, but the research-building code has not been reconciled to the institute's visiting address or demised labs. Do not pin a K-420 laboratory roof at 141 by assumption. [KS21] [KS22]

Swiss Life is a Klybeck landowner, while **Swiss Life Asset Management AG** is the campus contact at K-141. Rhystadt is the other landowner and the FLOW project operator, with a published contact in **WKL-136.EG, Klybeckstrasse 191**. For Stücki, primary Swiss Prime Site project material provides development/landlord evidence, and the live campus contact identifies **Wincasa AG** as centre and mixed-use site management, with **Equans** for technical facility management. None substitutes for parcel-specific title or an executed tenant lease. [KS14] [KS23] [KS24] [KS25] [KS26]

The JSON preserves the current Tech Park community directory separately, including biotech, medtech and discovery-engine residency labels. Those entries are not assigned the operator's 60C postal address. This distinction is material: the directory labels NBE **B2**, whereas NBE's current company/legal evidence supports **60I**. Possible stale or additional residency remains unresolved. The separate Stücki directory also lists TargImmune, but TargImmune's current company contact is **St. Alban-Anlage 70, 4052 Basel**, outside this northern corridor. It is therefore a conflicting/out-of-area lead, not a current verified Stücki company address. [KS20] [KS33] [KS34]

## Campus and building schedule

The **17 September 2026** Campus Klybeck schedule lists **K-25: 4,300 m²** office/storage/commercial, **K-141: 8,048 m²** office/coworking/commercial and **K-410: 3,100 m²** laboratory/office. These are the campus's **“Total area” rental-programme figures**; no gross/net building definition or current vacant quantum is supplied. Named operating office users do not establish complete building occupancy. K-25's Apleona move is announced **from November 2026**, not confirmed completed on 4 November. K-141 is an office programme, not a blanket life-science laboratory allocation. [KS14] [KS15]

Rhystadt's current building schedule is more specific. **WKL-136** is marketed at **Klybeckstrasse 191** for immediate fitted office/lab occupation. Its first/second-floor headline is **approximately 2,600 m²**, while the detailed listings are **1,590 m² office/laboratory on the first floor** and **173 m² and 696 m² offices on the second**. The detailed rows total **2,459 m²**, not the rounded headline. Asking rent is **CHF 220/m²/year or on request**; exclusions, VAT, incentives and service charges are unknown. The marketed **3.2-metre ceiling height** and support/handling facilities are source specifications, not independently measured clear height or lab licensing. None of these available floors measures LifeMine or Monte Rosa's occupancy elsewhere in WKL-136. [KS27]

**WKL-132** uses the same marketed campus address and offers **4,168 m² rental space**, comprising **1,042 m² on each of the third through sixth floors**, at **CHF 200/m²/year asking rent**. It is fitted office space, not verified wet-lab stock. **WKL-121** markets **1,140 m²** of office/commercial space at **CHF 95/m²/year or on request**, with a stated fixed-term offer **until March 2028**. Its listed floor rows total **1,139 m²**. The offered term is not a current life-science company's lease expiry. Both addresses require an actual building/entrance crosswalk before plotting, because the property pages publish a common campus address. [KS28] [KS29]

For Stücki, Swiss Prime Site's **17 December 2024** account describes **Stücki Park II as completed**, with **28,000 m² usable floor space** for laboratory and office uses. That is a defined extension-project measure, not whole-campus stock, current leased area or available inventory. Separate property records retain verified **60A, 60C, 60E, 60F, 60G and 60I** addresses, plus the current operator's **60B, Hochbergerstrasse 70 and Badenstrasse 3** offer titles. No aggregate tenant area is allocated between them. [KS11] [KS32]

## Development pipeline and availability evidence

**FLOW** is Rhystadt's refurbishment and extension of an existing lab/office building, with a current **approximately 19,000 m² future laboratory-and-office programme**. The primary German project timeline expects **construction start in 2027** and **occupation in Q3 2029**. Its captions refer to **Klybeck 125**, but a verified street address and unique entrance were not established. Future-phase prose in the English version says “construction underway” and “ready”; it should not be misread as a present completed status. Planned up-to-BSL-2 research uses, utility provision to tenancy boundaries and a **LEED Gold target** are advertised project specifications, not operating licences or achieved certification. The dated **26 October 2026** Rhystadt article supports reuse/extension, not completion. [KS30] [KS31]

The supplied October 2025 brochure separately recorded an unnamed **19,000 sqm Rhystadt project opening mid-2028**. The current FLOW offer is the relevant live pipeline lead, but the brochure-to-building identity has not been proven. Retain both evidentiary records; do not silently assert a confirmed schedule delay for the identical asset.

The canton describes the wider klybeckplus project as **nearly 30 hectares of transformation land**, in its **26 November 2025** planning release, with Swiss Life and Rhystadt as landowners. That is land area, not lettable floorspace. The Richtprojekt is a basis for land-use planning; the canton expected the development plan and public consultation in **early 2027**. The supplied Campus Klybeck brochure's **885,000 m²** district figure, page 7, has **no defined area basis** and is not converted into inventory or land. Planned residents/jobs are not used as current workforce. [KS23]

The live Stücki operator inventory advertises a **901 m², level-7 laboratory at Hochbergerstrasse 60A**, described as **BSL2, fully fitted**, with occupation **by agreement**. It also lists a **3,000 m² second-floor HO70 offer**, labelled extended basic fit-out and associated with Lab Seventy imagery. The historical brochure's **10,000 m² Lab Seventy office/lab offer from 2026** remains a historical whole-programme claim, not verified current delivered lab space. The present floor offer cannot establish the larger programme's delivery. [KS32]

Stücki's online data need reconciliation before use in an underwriting schedule: the **HO60B level-1 row says 399 m²**, but the detail says **60A / 256 m²**; the level-4 row says **415 m²**, while its office detail says **413 m²**. Office whole-floor and partial-floor cards in 60F may overlap. Rent cells such as “CHF 590” have no visible denominator/period in the extracted table, so they are not converted to CHF/m²/year. The JSON retains encountered office-module and building offers, but no additive market vacancy, rent average or absorption measure. [KS32]

## Property due diligence

The immediate gating items are K-410 commissioning and permitted-use evidence; a current WKL-136 unit schedule that reconciles headline and floor rows; and corrected Stücki unit/area/rent-denominator data. Obtain source-occupier and lease-demise evidence before attributing any listed space to a giveback. Lonza needs a dated A/G lease plan and rent roll to reconcile the current facility callout and historical building statements. NBE and Superlab need separate 60I floor boundaries, rather than summed facility figures.

FLOW requires the permit decision, start-of-works proof, building/parcel/address crosswalk and dated delivery programme. IOB requires its K-420 research entrance/lease crosswalk. Lab Seventy requires a current whole-project programme, technical standard and completion/available-unit schedule. Request parcel-specific title, contaminated-site and building-remediation reports, and intended-use restrictions. The canton explicitly identifies contamination-related removal of some buildings in the wider plan; that does not certify the suitability of any retained laboratory. [KS23]

For each occupier, company-occupied area, local workforce, legal contracting entity, leased versus owned interest, suite/floor, effective rent, expiry/options, floor loading, clear heights, ventilation, power/redundancy and manufacturing capacity remain unknown unless separately stated above. Source-labelled marketed specifications are not inspected capabilities. The operator directories support further address diligence, not an exhaustive verified company universe.

## Submarket aerials

Retain `basel-klybeck-stucki-klybeck`, `basel-klybeck-stucki-stuecki` and `basel-supplemental-bioversys-basel`. Existing aerials were retrieved **2 November 2026**, but their acquisition dates are not exposed; they are not live images. The existing Klybeck unit contains LifeMine and K-25 orientation references. The retained Stücki frame is **context-only with no company rows** and its southern edge is north of the V6 resolved 60-series company address points. It needs southward reframing and point QA before it can serve as street-level occupier coverage in the app or print set.

No new street pins were invented here. Shared campus addresses at 191 and 141, Lonza's grouped A/G address and FLOW's unverified street address must not be plotted as multiple precise roofs. The parent integration team should use the existing source-address records and new verified references, preserve IDs, and disclose the aerial-vintage gap. The shared application, masters and aerial files were not modified by this research.

## Source and coverage notes
Public primary pages were observed on 4 November 2026 unless marked as supplied recent evidence. NBE's same-day verified primary findings are reused from the supplied V6 correction. Historical internal sources are cited by title, date and page above; **no original brochure, private file or brochure image is included in this output**. The full JSON contains source visibility, quantity scope, publication/as-of, area basis, statuses and the complete encountered inventory.

clusters.detailedNarrative:
# Schällemätteli / university hospital research campus  -  Basel-Stadt

Schällemätteli is an occupied academic and clinical research district, with further institution-led construction, rather than an evidenced multi-tenant commercial laboratory leasing campus. Biozentrum and ETH’s BSS are operational; the existing Pharmazentrum, university hospital and children’s hospital remain distinct buildings and operators. The Department of Biomedicine’s new building is under construction, and the BRCCH office project is a separate pipeline asset. No source-backed commercial-company tenancy within this district was established in the supplied extracts, retained V6 address inventory or primary sources reviewed. This is an evidence gap, not a claim that no companies operate here. [RH01] [RH02] [RH03] [RH04] [RH05] [RH06]

Canton **BS**, municipality **Basel**. Research observed **4 November 2026**. The geographical frame is the retained analytical aerial unit `basel-research-campus-core`, not a surveyed campus boundary or an ownership parcel. University institutions and hospitals are not added to commercial-company counts. The supplied JLL hub extract distinguishes this district from Allschwil Main Campus, Novartis Campus, Klybeck/Stücki and Rosental/Roche; its research-campus logos are orientation evidence only. Internal source date is PDF metadata **31 October 2025**, not a printed publication date; relevant pages are 1, 20 and 24. No original private brochure is included in these outputs.

## Occupier inventory

**Biozentrum, University of Basel  -  Spitalstrasse 41, 4056 Basel.** Its current contact page verifies the address; the institution says it moved into the new building in 2021. It combines molecular-biology research laboratories and technology platforms with teaching, university IT infrastructure and public catering. These functions make the total building area different from a laboratory department’s exclusive occupied area. The retained V6 profile and site ID are both `basel-research-campus:anchor:biozentrum-university-of-basel`. They remain institutional references, not company leases. [RH01] [RH02] [RH07]

**ETH Zurich, Department of Biosystems Science and Engineering  -  BSS, Klingelbergstrasse 48, 4056 Basel.** Schanzenstrasse 44 is separately identified as its delivery address, not an additional occupier building. The research mix includes experimental biology, bioengineering, bioinformatics and computational analysis. ETH’s opening release documents a cleanroom and a GMP facility capable of preparing active substances, including reprogrammed cells, for clinical use or human trials. It does not establish a commercial manufacturing capacity, a leasable GMP suite or a current production licence. The retained V6 profile and site ID are `basel-research-campus:anchor:eth-zurich-d-bsse-building-bss`. [RH03] [RH08] [RH09]

**University of Basel, Department of Pharmaceutical Sciences  -  Pharmazentrum, Klingelbergstrasse 50, 4056 Basel.** This is the department’s current main building, not a new pipeline asset. The Department of Biomedicine also identifies research accommodation in the Pharmazentrum at **Klingelbergstrasse 50/70**, explicitly on the **seventh floor**, with brain ageing/neurodegeneration, neuroplasticity and hearing research groups. This is a source-stated floor location; there is no disclosed DBM-exclusive floor area. The address range must not be turned into two independent occupied buildings, nor confused with the future DBM building carrying the planned address Klingelbergstrasse 70. Neither department has a matched V6 institution profile in the snapshot reviewed; both are retained as additional institutional leads, without creating global-company IDs. [RH04] [RH10]

**University of Basel, Department of Biomedicine  -  Hebelstrasse 20, 4031 Basel.** This is an existing research location with named groups in tissue/cartilage engineering, immunology, cancer biology, infection biology, human genomics and clinical translational research. It is not evidence that those functions have already moved to the new DBM building. The department’s locations index still lists several city locations; the new-build project explicitly describes consolidation of a dispersed institution. Existing premises’ leasehold interests, occupied areas and future releases are not disclosed. [RH11] [RH12] [RH05]

**University Hospital Basel  -  Klinikum 1 entrance, Spitalstrasse 21; existing Klinikum 2 entrance, Petersgraben 4; institutional postal code 4031 Basel.** The operator verifies each entrance separately. These addresses do not define the hospital estate boundary. USB provides inpatient and outpatient care, clinical teaching and research. Its retained V6 profile/site ID is `basel-research-campus:anchor:university-hospital-basel`; V6 contains an empty address even though the retained primary-source record supplies the paired entrances. This detail is resolved here only; the snapshot is unchanged. [RH06] [RH13]

**University Children’s Hospital Basel  -  UKBB, Spitalstrasse 33, Basel.** Its current institutional page confirms an independent university centre for paediatric/adolescent medicine, teaching and research. The official canton building page identifies the physical address as **4056 Basel**; the operator page also uses **4031 Basel** for contact. Retain the street and number, and distinguish physical from institutional postal codes rather than create separate sites. UKBB occupied this building in January 2011; no new 2026 move is established. It has no matched V6 profile in the reviewed snapshot. [RH14] [RH15]

**Hospital and university pharmacy/research buildings.** The university’s location directory and research-group pages identify the **Rossetti building, Spitalstrasse 26, 4031 Basel**, for Hospital Pharmacy and the Clinical Pharmacy & Epidemiology group head’s office; the **Formonterhof, St. Johanns-Vorstadt 27, 4031 Basel**, accommodates that group’s postdoctoral/doctoral and programming work. This is pharmacoepidemiology and clinical medicines research, not proof of wet labs at Formonterhof. **Schanzenstrasse 55, 4031 Basel** is the verified Clinical Pharmacology & Toxicology address, with drug-information/pharmacovigilance and psychopharmacology research. No floor area, cleanroom class or clinical manufacturing capacity is disclosed for these addresses. [RH04] [RH16] [RH17]

**Basel Research Centre for Child Health  -  BRCCH, current offices at Petersgraben 31, 4051 Basel.** Its own directions page describes offices there. The current contact office is kept separate from the future research-centre building. BRCCH is supported by the University of Basel and ETH Zurich, with partner institutions including UKBB and Swiss TPH; partnership does not establish that each partner occupies the BRCCH office. There is no matched V6 profile. [RH18] [RH19]

## Campus and building schedule

**Biozentrum property area and ownership.** Basel-Stadt’s handover release, published **25 January 2021**, records **23,400 m² Hauptnutzfläche** for the entire new Biozentrum building and names **University of Basel as owner** at handover. The live institution facts page, publication date unstated and observed **4 November 2026**, again gives **23,400 m²**, but labels it only **Nutzfläche**. The magnitude is reconfirmed; the more precise historical measurement label should be retained until the current area schedule is supplied. It is neither total campus land nor Biozentrum-exclusive leased laboratory area. The historical release also describes university IT services and the university-wide data centre in the building. Current registered title and allocation by user require property documentation. [RH07] [RH20]

**BSS areas and tenure.** ETH’s current architectural tour, publication date unstated and observed **4 November 2026**, states **5,000 m² wet laboratories** and **600 m² scientific facilities** within BSS. These are functional components, not the total building, a third-party lease or available space; do not sum them into department occupancy. The same page says the pentagonal building covers **4,180 m²**, without defining a cadastral, gross-floor or net-area standard. Retain that statement as an undefined building-covering area, not verified land area. ETH’s property project says it built BSS under a **Baurecht**; the **Einwohnergemeinde der Stadt Basel owns the land**. The building is ETH’s facility, but the leasehold term, reversion provisions and financial obligations are not disclosed. [RH08] [RH09]

BSS’s project chronology distinguishes **2023 handover, laboratory fit-out and start of teaching** from the **16 May 2024 ceremonial opening**. There is no need to choose one as an all-purpose completion date. The architectural tour documents a subterranean logistics connection with Biozentrum and UKBB. Its reference to a DBM connection in 2028 is older programme language; it is not adopted as the new DBM’s delivery date. [RH08] [RH09] [RH03] [RH05]

**Other existing buildings.** Pharmazentrum, Hebelstrasse 20, hospital entrance buildings, UKBB, Rossetti, Formonterhof, Schanzenstrasse 55 and Petersgraben 31 have verified institutional addresses/functions as described above, but no adopted current area schedule or registered ownership evidence in this review. The UKBB historical project page documents construction and January 2011 occupation, not a current lettable area. No campus aggregate is calculated from this mixed schedule. [RH04] [RH10] [RH11] [RH13] [RH14] [RH15] [RH16] [RH17] [RH18]

## Development pipeline

**New DBM building  -  planned address Klingelbergstrasse 70, Basel.** University of Basel is the developer; Implenia is total contractor and Burckhardt Architektur general planner. The current university project page describes **over 35,000 m² Geschossfläche** in its text and **35,000 m² Gesamtfläche** in its facts panel. Record this as a planned building floor-area figure, not net laboratory, department-exclusive occupancy or leasable space. The building is intended to bring currently dispersed DBM research groups together. The former Biozentrum building was demolished in **2022**; new construction began in **September 2023**. The live schedule records shell completion in **2025**, fit-out **2026–2029**, building completion **2029**, commissioning **2030** and relocation **2031**. These distinct stages were observed **4 November 2026** on an undated current university page. They are not a vacant-space delivery or a confirmed release of existing DBM buildings. [RH05]

**BRCCH new office/research-centre building  -  corner of Schanzenstrasse and Spitalstrasse.** The canton’s **15 October 2025** announcement scheduled construction start for **30 October 2025**, existing-building demolition through **spring 2026**, and completion by **end 2027**. It explicitly describes an office building, with digital paediatric medicine as the institutional focus; it is not a wet-lab or GMP offering. Guerra Clauss is the architect and Immobilien Basel-Stadt the client. The architect’s project entry, publication date unstated and observed **4 November 2026**, states **2,146 m² GF**; GF is not expanded and is not converted into net lettable or occupied area. The public sources read do not establish a verified numbered project address or a 2026 construction milestone, so the location stays a corner reference and completion remains the dated announced target. Do not attach the current Petersgraben 31 address to the planned building. [RH19] [RH21]

**New Klinikum 2  -  USB Campus Gesundheit.** The official canton project page, observed **4 November 2026** with no publication date stated, says the first stage started in **2024** and is expected to be operational **2033**; the second stage is planned **2035–2042**. The operator’s current page gives an overall completion horizon of **2042** but retains an older FAQ with a first phase **2024–2030** and replacement work to **2038**. Use the canton’s operational target provisionally and obtain USB’s controlled current schedule before investment or relocation decisions. [RH06] [RH22]

A dated USB update of **24 September 2026** confirms physical construction: the underground annex had reached full structural height and the bed tower had reached its second above-ground floor. The annex is intended to house intervention radiology; the operator’s project page describes emergency, endoscopy, ambulatory and inpatient functions in the first phase. These are hospital-use development, not commercial laboratory leasing inventory. The tower’s final structural height is targeted for **end 2027** in the September update, not operational completion. No adopted gross/net floor-area number is used here. [RH23] [RH06]

**Klinikum 3  -  not retained as an active delivered-space offer.** The current canton page expressly says USB is foregoing its previously planned new Klinikum 3. This is direct project-decision evidence, not a closure inference from the Claraspital transaction and not evidence that any existing hospital site is closing. An older February 2025 reduction-to-podium announcement remains linked on the operator’s page; it should not be presented as the current active pipeline without confirmation. The canton page contains a malformed integration year; that year is not reproduced as a factual deadline. [RH22] [RH06]

## Availability evidence

No current third-party laboratory or office availability, vacant suite, asking rent, lease expiry or marketed term was established for this district. All building areas above describe existing institutional property or planned building components, not market vacancy. Cooperation with companies, shared equipment access and public catering do not establish third-party tenancy.

The near-term property enquiry is therefore institutional: clarify whether any department’s consolidation creates releasable premises, whether the institutions can license shared research infrastructure, and whether title/leasehold arrangements permit third-party use. These are due-diligence questions, not sourced offers. In particular, DBM’s planned relocation is not a confirmed giveback at Hebelstrasse 20 or Pharmazentrum.

## Property due diligence

1. Obtain a controlled **building and space register** from University of Basel Immobilien, distinguishing parcel land area, gross floor area, Hauptnutzfläche, laboratory area and user allocation. Reconcile Biozentrum’s historical Hauptnutzfläche with the current generic Nutzfläche label. Obtain Pharmazentrum and Hebelstrasse 20 schedules rather than allocate university aggregates to DBM.
2. Obtain **title and Baurecht extracts**: University of Basel’s Biozentrum interest; ETH’s BSS building interest and municipal land title; DBM and BRCCH site ownership; and registered ownership/tenure of USB and UKBB buildings. For BSS, request term, extension rights, reversion, permitted use and obligations; no term is assumed.
3. Request the **current DBM project baseline** and move schedule from `neubau-dbm@unibas.ch`, including commissioning versus user occupation, planned phasing by origin building, premises retained, and any consented release. Confirm whether the architectural-tour tunnel timetable has been superseded.
4. Request **BRCCH’s numbered new-building address, current works certificate, approved area schedule and occupation date** from Immobilien Basel-Stadt and BRCCH. Confirm whether the architect’s GF figure covers the whole final project and whether any laboratory functions are actually in scope.
5. Request the **current Klinikum 2 stage schedule** from `campus.gesundheit@usb.ch`, reconciling the current canton timeline with the older FAQ. Ask for stage-by-stage clinical space, temporary accommodation, retained buildings and approved Klinikum 3 decision; do not infer hospital closure from an acquisition.
6. Obtain **facility-specific capability records** only where a user or transaction requires them: BSS GMP authorisation/operating entity, cleanroom classification and service-access rights; biosafety levels, permitted hazardous work, HVAC redundancy, vibration and floor-load specifications for each relevant building. A research institute’s capability cannot be inherited by neighbouring buildings.
7. Obtain a **third-party occupier/licence register** and a dated availability schedule from the relevant institutional property teams. Until then, commercial occupants, rents, suite sizes, lease dates, local FTE and vacancy remain unknown. A documented property/occupier denominator is required before calling this inventory exhaustive.

## Submarket aerials

The existing public-imagery exhibit is retained, not regenerated:

![Retained SWISSIMAGE aerial context for Schällemätteli and the university hospital district; not live construction evidence]([retained internal document]

Unit **`basel-research-campus-core`** uses SWISSIMAGE, **© swisstopo**, retrieved **2 November 2026**. Acquisition vintage is not exposed and must not be inferred from retrieval. The retained exhibit locates only Biozentrum and BSS institutional address references; it does not yet pin the newly documented building inventory. The paired hospital entrances have no unique retained point. Exact street-address inventory is supplied in the companion JSON, but new building pins, footprints and parcel outlines require official address/cadastral matching and visual QA by the integrating team. Neither an aerial outline nor a street address establishes tenant space or ownership. The existing image and exhibit remain unchanged.

## Coverage and evidence gaps

The reviewed source set supports the addresses identified here, not every possible occupant in the canton. The supplied JLL study and EMEA extracts have no building-level campus area or tenancy schedule. No private-company campus occupier was established; broad Basel peers in V6 cannot be placed here from city context. Mattenstrasse university locations belong to Rosental and are not reclassified into this district. The Pharmacy Museum at Totengässlein 3 is a sourced museum location, not a life-science R&D occupier, and is excluded from the operating laboratory inventory. BRCCH’s Petersgraben office is retained as an institutional-office reference at the medical-district edge.

All undisclosed occupied/leased areas, land areas, workforce, lease expiries, rents, commercial vacancies and building technical specifications remain **unknown**, not zero. There is no confirmed area-based leasing opportunity or timing in this cluster. The JSON retains separate institutions, existing buildings, planned developments, address aliases, source dates and metric bases, with the V6 anchors unchanged.
